title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Keepalive Scheduler Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, adjacent RFC 9220 regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel with a configured keepalive interval. The client observes an automatic server ping, sends a pong, sends later text data, and receives the handler response on the same tunnel.
preconditions: The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
Manual ping helper behavior remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0008`.
Handler-failure close behavior remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0009`.
expected_result: The focused loopback and regression tests pass, the new RFC 9220 keepalive requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server handler path now has locally verified opt-in keepalive ping scheduling on accepted RFC 9220 tunnels while preserving later tunnel data. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
